spots.name: Suomenlinna (Sveaborg / Fortress of Finland)
spots.description: An 18th-century sea fortress built across six islands at the mouth of Helsinki's harbour, begun under Swedish rule in 1748 and a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1991. Around 800 people still live there year-round. Bloggers suggest taking the regular public HSL ferry from Market Square and packing a picnic for the southern ramparts.

spots.name: Oodi (Helsinki Central Library)
spots.description: Helsinki's central library, opened in December 2018 to mark the centenary of Finnish independence, with a wave-shaped spruce facade designed by ALA Architects. Besides books it lends out sewing machines, 3D printers and recording studios. Locals recommend the top-floor 'book heaven' and its terrace facing the Parliament House.

spots.name: Temppeliaukion kirkko (Rock Church)
spots.description: A Lutheran church carved directly into solid granite, completed in 1969 by architects Timo and Tuomo Suomalainen. A copper dome and a ring of skylights let daylight in along the rock walls. Bloggers recommend going early to avoid tour groups and checking for concerts, as the acoustics are excellent.
